newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia forms new airline with Thai partner.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia forms new airline with Thai partner.

text.p: The Cambodian government and Orient Thai Airlines have formed a joint venture to operate a new airline, company officials said on Tuesday.
Kampuchea Airlines will begin service by next week, said Orient Thai Managing Director Udom Tantiprasongchai.
He did not provide further details on the deal, only saying the Cambodian government held the majority stake.
Kampuchea Airlines will provide service to Bangkok, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, Hong Kong and Guangzhou, officials said.
It will be the second Cambodian airline. Royal Air Cambodge (RAC), a joint venture between the government and Malaysia Helicopter Services, is Cambodia's flag carrier.

Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who ousted rival co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh earlier this month, broke RAC's monopoly status soon after taking sole power and declared an "open skies" policy in the country.
Malaysia Helicopter Services officials have warned they may pull out of Cambodia if another carrier is brought in.
"RAC wants a monopoly, but now the government has an open skies policy. So far, we aren't sure if RAC will pull out or not," said Keo Sophal, director general of the Cambodia Aviation Authority.

For Tantiprasongchai, the situation is a reversal of the one he faced in 1994, when he operated a private airline in Cambodia, Cambodian International Airlines (CIA), a senior government official said.

CIA was abruptly shut down in December 1994 by the government when it formed RAC, which was a partnership between the state airline operating at the time, Kampuchea Airlines, and Malaysian Helicopter Services.
